name: Act Declaration
definition: Holds each declared act on the outside world, with the external service that it reaches, the form of its arguments and the writer that declared it. Accepts the declaration of an act, a change to an act and the removal of an act.
rationale: DEC-069 puts the acts in this system, and DEC-103 makes the declaration of an act on the outside world the statement of what the platform must know about that act. The acts that another system holds are fixed by the design of that system and are not declared here (DEC-111). REQ-PL-031 gives each declaration a new, a change and a removal, so the three are one capability, as FUN-AU-01 states for a class. DEC-076 makes this a declaration, because this system refuses a call to an act on the outside world that is not declared.

name: Act Interface
definition: Gives a caller the acts that its position admits, accepts a call to each of them, carries an act that another system holds to that system, and gives the caller the result.
rationale: DEC-111 makes this system the one interface through which a caller reaches every act, so the set that a caller sees is the set that it can call, and the classification of REQ-PL-012 and the record of REQ-PL-014 are at one point for each act on the outside world. DEC-069 makes this system hold the acts, including the act that gives the set of acts, and REQ-AD-052 states in the rules where a caller finds them. To give only the acts that a position admits keeps the context of an agent small, and it is not a refusal: FUN-AC-03 refuses. The system that holds an act refuses what a position does not admit and does the act, so this function adds no judgement (DEC-030). The first text held the description and the call in two functions, and they are one interface.

name: Admission by Position
definition: Refuses a call to an act on the outside world, and the declaration, the change or the removal of an act, from a caller whose position does not admit it.
rationale: DEC-019 declares the position in one place and makes each boundary refuse, and DEC-029 makes an act any operation that a boundary refuses. This system holds the acts on the outside world, so it is the boundary for them. FUN-WC-05, FUN-ST-07 and FUN-AU-03 are the same function at the other boundaries. A list that does not show an act does not refuse a call to it (DEC-111).

name: Classification at the Call
definition: Gives Authorization each act on the outside world that a caller calls, with its arguments. Refuses an act that is in a declared class unless the act arrives released with an affirmative answer of the user to a request that states it.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 refuses an action that needs authorization until the platform records an affirmative answer. DEC-103 has Authorization judge the act with its arguments and not the act alone, because a message to the user and a message to a third party are one act with two objects. DEC-104 has this system refuse and the caller raise the request, so the raiser keeps the time of the act (DEC-108). DEC-108 sends every released gated unit here, so the answer is checked against the act at one point. DEC-110 states what an act on the outside world does when Authorization gives no answer. The holder of an act inside the platform gates it (DEC-111).

name: External Action
definition: Does each admitted act on the outside world through External Access, and gives the result of each gated act, or that its call returned no result, to Work and Coordination.
rationale: FUN-PL-08. DEC-107 makes this system the only one that refuses what reaches outside the platform, and External Access carries the call and holds the credentials. DEC-066 has the system that acts on the outside world do a gated action, and REQ-WC-070 closes the gated unit with the result that this system gives.

name: Action Record
definition: Gives, for each act on the outside world that it does, the act with its arguments, the agent that called it or raised its gated unit, the time, the authority and the result, to be recorded.
rationale: REQ-PL-014. This system holds no body under DEC-024, so DEC-106 holds the record in Self-Observation as data about the platform. The authority is stated as the unit of work that holds the answer and is not copied, so one answer of the user has one record (DEC-019).
